about: Every outside site you touch, and the rail you OWN to each: read / search / post. kind = api (your own OAuth or key) | feed (public JSON/RSS/rehydration payload) | page (fetch + parse) | browser (a real Chrome with your own profile, via browserd.py) | human (a person does it) | none. post rails are ALWAYS human-fired: door.py refuses to run one without --human-fired "<the user's words>", which it logs. Nothing here evades a site's defences: a shut door is reported with the human step that opens it. Edit this file; leave door.py alone.

read.note: YouTube Data API on your own OAuth refresh token (youtube_token.json, scope youtube.force-ssl)

post.note: replies from a fire sheet; dry run without --post; link-carrying replies may be filtered silently -- read them back

probe.means: exit 2 = OAuth refresh worked, no verb given

reddit.human_step: create the script app once and add REDDIT_CLIENT_ID / REDDIT_CLIENT_SECRET / REDDIT_USERNAME / REDDIT_PASSWORD to your environment
